Exercise: Side Laterals to Front Raise

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- front_raise
- unilateral_shoulder_abduction

Primary Muscles:

- shoulders

Secondary Muscles:

- traps

Equipment:

- dumbbell

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.75

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- trap_activation
- shoulder_strength_and_hypertrophy

Contraindications:

- Shoulder instability or injury
- Rotator cuff issues

Exercise Variations:

- name: Single-Arm Side Lateral to Front Raise, notes: Use a single dumbbell for each arm.
- name: Machine Side Lateral to Front Raise, equipment: cable machine

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Lateral Raises, equipment: dumbbell or cable
- exercise_name: Front Raise, equipment: dumbbell or barbell

Instructions:

- In a standing position, hold a pair of dumbbells at your side. This will be your starting position.
- Keeping your elbows slightly bent, raise the weights directly in front of you to shoulder height, avoiding any swinging or cheating.
- At the top of the exercise move the weights out in front of you, keeping your arms extended.
- Lower the weights with a controlled motion.
- On the next repetition, raise the weights in front of you to shoulder height before moving the weights laterally to your sides.
- Lower the weights to the starting position.
